findings.claim: In the measured code nothing applies core.clj's :inline. The codemod only decides whether to strip it (jolt keeps it) and then emits the call unchanged. jolt's compiler never reads :inline, and it inlines a call only when the head resolves to a clojure.core var. So in a stock namespace, (< i n), (inc i), (* i 2) and (+ a b) are ordinary calls of the booted cohost.core vars. The JVM host is the control: there the JVM compiler applies the same booted vars' :inline, and loop-arith runs at the same speed on the stock and host sides.

findings.claim: Inside each stock fn, the arity body calls a shim var whose value is jolt's value-position proc. For +, *, < and = that proc is variadic. Every call conses a rest list (2 pairs for + and *, 1 for <), tests for a boxed lazy rest, and folds over the binary helper (fold-left for + and *, a loop for <). Numbers-inc (jolt-inc) and Numbers-unchecked_inc (jolt-uncinc) are fixed-arity. cohost adds no overflow check and no type dispatch: jolt-add2 is a number? test followed by Chez's generic +, so a long overflow widens to a bignum where the JVM's Numbers.add throws. jolt-lt2 is a number? test followed by <. Numbers-minus is the only one written as a fixed-arity fn, and jolt compiles it to a case-lambda with jolt-n- inline.

findings.claim: Those two call layers per arithmetic op account for both ratios. A stock defn adds no wrapper. core.clj's defn expands to (def name (fn ...)). The codemod's def rewrite only merges :def-meta, which is nil on jolt. The boot's macro wrapping rewrites expansions at compile time only. So bench-inc costs the same var call on both sides, and fn-call's extra time is the 3 stock ops (< and inc in the loop, + inside bench-inc).

findings.claim: At HEAD, the `(.swap atom f x)` in stock swap! became `((cohost.shim/dot "swap" cohost.shim/-swap) atom f x)`. So every swap! did three things. First, it built a new 5-arity dispatcher closure. jolt registers the closure's variadic arity under a mutex in a weak hashtable each time one is created. Second, it asked the adapter's uncached user-type?: a cap lookup, a string built by (str (class x)), then .startsWith and .contains. Third, it went through -swap to jolt's swap!, which calls the stock + (both layers plus the variadic fold). There is no check-cast, because clojure.lang.IAtom is not in checked-hints. dotimes adds a stock < and a stock unchecked-inc. Measured (quoted run): 1969 ns per iteration on the stock side against 48 on the host. Building the dispatcher once (dot$swap) and caching own? per class in the working tree cut this to 920 ns per iteration (target/bench-jolt.edn at 14:43). So about 1050 ns per iteration was the per-call construction plus the uncached user-type?.

findings.claim: With the dispatcher prebuilt (the 14:43 run), the remaining cost of own? was computing the cache key. On jolt v0.8.23, (class an-atom) has no fast path: class-fast-name has no atom arm, and jolt-class-name has no last-value memo, so it walks every registered class arm before jolt-class-base answers clojure.lang.Atom. Then jolt-class-for string-hashes the name, and jolt-get hashes the class token (hash-arm walk plus a murmur of the name) after a deref of the cache atom through a var call (deref is not a jolt native op). The working tree has since added an adapter :host-data? early-out (jolt: transient?, atom?, fn?, ...) ahead of the class lookup. With it, the 14:53 run shows 161 ns per iteration against 54.6 on the host (x3.0). What remains is the call chain: stock swap!, dot$swap, own?, h-host-data?, -swap, jolt swap!, stock +. The host side makes one call to jolt swap!.

findings.claim: Every cohost layer is compiled at runtime with jolt's call-site tracing on. It is on by default and nothing in cohost sets JOLT_TRACE. Tracing wraps each non-tail call in a virtual-register save and restore, and stores a site pair before a named fn's tail call. jolt's own core is precompiled and pays none of this. Stock paths have many more runtime-compiled call layers than host paths, so tracing inflates only the stock side. That confound matters most for atom-swap. Before pass 1 it also added 4 wrapped calls per iteration to the stock loop-arith thunk; the host thunk has none.

findings.claim: Pass 1 in the working tree applies :inline at rewrite time and emits host core symbols for shim statics that are host fns. It had not reached host speed in the 14:53 run: loop-arith went from 27.4 ms to 10.43 ms (x19), fn-call from 10.7 ms to 5.49 ms (x3.4). That run's alias table matched shim values to host var roots by identity, keeping the first var found. In jolt v0.8.23, +' and +, *' and *, and inc' and inc share one proc each, so Numbers-add could alias to clojure.core/+', which jolt does not inline. That would turn 3 of the 4 ops back into var calls, 2 of them into variadic procs, while < (no primed twin) is open-coded. This fits the measured 52 ns per iteration. The working tree's boot.cljc now prefers the shortest name, compiled at 15:05 after that run. One correctness gap is still open: inline-expansion trusts *locals*, which does not include deftype/defrecord fields or reify/deftype/extend method params, nor names bound by when-first, areduce, amap or bound-fn.

fixes.change: Finish the rewrite-time :inline pass with host aliases (already in the working tree: rewrite.cljc inline-expansion and rw-static's (:host-aliases ctx) lookup; boot.cljc inline-fn and host-aliases; jolt.clj :rewrite-inline? true). A stock (h args), where h resolves to a cohost.core var whose :inline covers the arity, becomes its expansion. A shim static whose value is a host core var's root is emitted as that host symbol, marked :cohost/host so restock leaves it alone. On jolt, (+ acc (* i 2)) becomes (clojure.core/+ acc (clojure.core/* i 2)), which jolt lowers to jolt-n+ and jolt-n*. Keep the deterministic alias choice (plain name over +', *', inc'), and confirm it with probe 1. Before relying on *locals* for inlining, add method params and deftype/defrecord fields to *locals* in rw-method-clause and rw-spec-form, and add when-first, areduce, amap and bound-fn to binding-heads.
fixes.removes: Per arithmetic op: both cached var calls (the stock case-lambda and the shim var), the variadic rest-list cons with fold-left or the cmp-chain loop (jolt-add, jolt-mul, jolt-lt), and the jolt-truthy? around comparisons. Stock call sites compile to the host's own open-coded jolt-n< / jolt-n-inc / jolt-n* / jolt-n+ (or jolt-l*), as the JVM compiler does with the same metadata (bench-clj loop-arith: stock 0.0879 ms, host 0.0880 ms). This also open-codes dotimes's < and unchecked-inc in atom-swap, and the 2-arity body of the stock + that swap! calls.
fixes.risk: (a) A field or param named like an inlinable core fn (inc, max, min, count, nth, int, num ...) and called as a fn inside a deftype, defrecord, reify or extend body would be inlined as the core fn, until *locals* covers those binders. (b) with-redefs or alter-var-root of +, < or inc no longer reaches compiled call sites; the JVM behaves the same way. (c) *unchecked-math* is read at rewrite time, also as on the JVM. (d) Every :inline in core.clj now applies (count, nth, int, long, =, compare, bit ops, aget ...), so the battery and corpus must be re-run. (e) Boot-time cost: one ns-resolve per call head. (f) An alias is only as good as root identity, and a host that rebinds a var root later (as jolt's float.ss and bigdec.ss re-def inc) can break the match silently. Probe 1 shows what was emitted.

If a narrower patch is wanted: (not (h-atom? x)) at the top of host-object?, where h-atom? is the adapter's :atom? already looked up once (shim.cljc:35).
fixes.removes: Per swap!: jolt v0.8.23's (class an-atom), which walks every registered class arm with no memo in that release, then jolt-class-for's string hash; also the deref of the cache atom through a var call, and the jolt-get keyed by a class token (hash-arm walk plus a murmur of the class name). All of it is replaced by (instance? clojure.lang.Atom x), which jolt answers from a per-site inline cache keyed by ref-kind.
fixes.risk: Low. :host-data? must never answer true for a user type. A deftype implementing clojure.lang.IAtom is not an instance of the concrete clojure.lang.Atom, so it still reaches its own .swap. java.clj:84-85 already treats every 'class clojure.*' value as non-user. Each host's :atom? must stay a concrete-type test.

fixes.change: Pass 2: give swap!, reset!, compare-and-set!, swap-vals! and reset-vals! a host native with the stock path as fallback. A policy replacement whose arities read (if (h-atom? atom) (host-swap! atom f x) (.swap atom f x)), where host-swap! is the host core's swap! looked up once in the shim.
fixes.removes: Per swap!, the stock-only chain: stock swap!, dot$swap, own?, the :host-data? predicate calls, and -swap. That is about 5 runtime-compiled (and traced) calls, leaving one stock call and jolt's swap!.
fixes.risk: These names stop being core.clj's own text; they become policy replacements, as cast already is. Non-atoms keep the stock path, including user IAtom types and nil, which still gets the stock NPE. For real atoms, error text becomes the host's (jolt-need-atom). Re-run the battery's atoms, add-watch and doto rows, and the corpus iref/IAtom rows.

fixes.change: Run jolt benches with JOLT_TRACE=0 for both sides (bb.edn bench:jolt and run.cljc --bench), or record the env with the results and report both.
fixes.removes: The virtual-register save and restore jolt wraps around every non-tail call, plus the tail-site store, in runtime-compiled code. That means all of cohost.core, cohost.shim and the adapter, none of which jolt's precompiled core ever pays.
fixes.risk: No effect on values. An uncaught error in that run reports without tail-frame history.

fixes.change: Only on a host where fix 1's alias is not found: make the variadic-valued shim statics fixed-arity, with call-position bodies, the way Numbers-minus already is. For example (def Numbers-add (fn [x y] (+ x y))), (def Numbers-multiply (fn [x y] (* x y))), (def Numbers-lt (fn [x y] (< x y))), (def Util-equiv (fn [x y] (= x y))).
fixes.removes: The rest-list cons, the boxed-rest-seq test and the fold-left or cmp-chain loop of jolt's value-position procs, on each remaining shim call.
fixes.risk: Do not do this on jolt while fix 1 is in place. host-aliases matches a shim value against host var roots by identity, so a wrapper fn would switch the alias off and bring a shim call back. Numbers.add and lt are binary on the JVM, and core.clj only calls them with 2 args.

probes.tests: Diagnostic, not a timing; the printed form is the evidence. Expect (clojure.core/< i (clojure.core/+ acc (clojure.core/* (clojure.core/inc i) 2))) and true. If clojure.core/+', *' or inc' appear, the alias collision is still there. If (cohost.shim/Numbers-add ...) appears, the alias is missing. If (+ acc ...) is left unchanged, the call-site :inline is not applied, and the second value shows whether the :inline meta is a fn on jolt.

probes.form: (time (loop [i 0 acc 0] (if (< i 200000) (recur (inc i) (+ acc (* i 2))) acc)))
probes.tests: Tests the claim that loop-arith's whole gap is the arithmetic call sites. HEAD code took 27.4 to 28.5 ms (bench stock). With inline plus plain-name aliases it should reach the bench host time (0.50 to 0.54 ms). The 14:53 run's 10.43 ms is the 'inline plus primed alias' state. A result still well above 1 ms after the alias fix refutes the claim; run probe 1 to see why.

probes.form: (time (loop [i 0 acc 0] (if (cohost.shim/Numbers-lt i 200000) (recur (cohost.shim/Numbers-inc i) (cohost.shim/Numbers-add acc (cohost.shim/Numbers-multiply i 2))) acc)))
probes.tests: Times HEAD's inner layer alone: a cached var call into jolt's value-position procs, variadic for lt, add and multiply. Explicit cohost.shim/ symbols are not aliased by either tree, so it measures the same thing on both. If it is close to HEAD's 27 to 28 ms, the variadic procs dominate and the stock-fn layer is cheap. If it is about half, the two layers cost the same.

probes.form: (let [v cohost.shim/Numbers-add f cohost.shim/Numbers-minus] (time (loop [i 0 acc 0] (if (< i 200000) (recur (inc i) (v acc i)) acc))) (time (loop [i 0 acc 0] (if (< i 200000) (recur (inc i) (f acc i)) acc))))
probes.tests: Isolates the rest-list and fold cost. Both loops make the same local call per iteration. The first callee is jolt-add (variadic, what Numbers-add is); the second is Numbers-minus, a fixed-arity case-lambda with jolt-n- inline. Equal times would refute the claim that the variadic machinery matters per op.

probes.form: (let [f +] (time (loop [i 0 acc 0] (if (< i 200000) (recur (inc i) (f acc i)) acc))))
probes.tests: Times the stock + as a value, which is what (swap! a + i) and (reduce + ...) call. On HEAD it goes through the stock case-lambda, then Numbers-add, then variadic jolt-add, so it should be slower than probe 3's first line. With the plain-name alias, its 2-arity body is open-coded and it should match probe 3's second line. Staying near the first line means the stock fn body still reaches a variadic proc.

probes.form: (do (defn probe-id [x] x) (time (loop [i 0 acc 0] (if (< i 100000) (recur (inc i) acc) acc))) (time (loop [i 0 acc 0] (if (< i 100000) (recur (inc i) (probe-id acc)) acc))))
probes.tests: Tests the claim that a stock defn adds no wrapper. The second time minus the first is the cost of one call to a stock-defn'd fn. That difference should be close to the bench's host fn-call per-iteration time (1.57 to 1.71 ms per 100k, mostly that one var call). A much larger difference refutes 'no wrapping'.

probes.form: (let [a (atom 0)] (time (dotimes [i 100000] nil)) (time (dotimes [i 100000] (swap! a + i))) (time (dotimes [i 100000] (cohost.shim/dot$swap a + i))) (time (dotimes [i 100000] (cohost.shim/-swap a + i))) (time (dotimes [i 100000] (cohost.shim/host-object? a))) @a)
probes.tests: Decomposes atom-swap in the working tree (dot$swap does not exist at HEAD). Lines: (1) the loop alone; (2) the case; (3) skips the stock swap! layer; (4) skips the dispatcher and goes straight to jolt's swap! with the stock +; (5) the own? test alone. (2)-(3) is the stock swap! call, (3)-(4) is the dispatcher, and (5)-(1) is host-object? on an atom, which should be small now that :host-data? exists. If (2)-(4) is most of stock minus host (bench host about 4.7 to 5.5 ms), the call layers are what is left, and fix 3 is the one to make.

Reproduces HEAD's two atom-swap costs. Line 1 builds a new dispatcher per call (jolt registers its variadic arity under a mutex in a weak table); compare it with probe 7's line 3 (prebuilt dot$swap). Line 2 is HEAD's uncached own? test: jolt class of an atom (class-arm walk in v0.8.23), str, .startsWith and .contains. Together these should account for the drop from 196.87 ms (quoted) to 92.05 ms (14:43 run). Small values would refute that attribution.

Tests the tracing confound. Run it in the default environment and again with JOLT_TRACE=0 set for the jolt process; that env var is the only switch. jolt v0.8.23 traces all runtime-compiled code (all of cohost) and none of its own core. Equal times refute the confound. A clear drop under JOLT_TRACE=0 means stock-only layers are inflated relative to host calls, and both bench sides should run with JOLT_TRACE=0.
